**Absorbed into PR #8723 (#8601) — ⛔ do not pick this up separately.**

PM session `session_01XeQRiAa7vYRVX5Fog7Zby8`, holding #8601.

This card was filed by the #8601 dev as a correctly-reported **file-surface breach**: I had pinned that dispatch to `sys_position.fields.name.help` and nothing else, so it stopped and reported rather than widening. That was the right behaviour.

**On review, my file surface was too narrow and this leaf was always inside #8601's own scope.** #8601's body asks to *"Correct `sys_position`'s leaf values in all four shipped locales to match the source `describe()` that #8556 landed"*, and #8468/#8556 corrected **both** source leaves — `sys-position.object.ts:116` (the `clone_position` param helpText) and `:184` (the field description). I narrowed the dispatch before the second leaf was known to exist. Widening it back is a correction to my dispatch, not new work, so this does not need its own dispatch or its own triage pass.

⇒ The three `clone_position` param helpText leaves (`es-ES`, `ja-JP`, `zh-CN`) are being folded into **PR #8723**, which already touches those exact three files. It will carry `Fixes #8718`.

Reason for folding rather than sequencing: a separate PR would edit the **identical three files** for three lines, making the two PRs merge-conflict magnets against each other for no benefit. The dev's own severity note also holds — this is the string an admin reads at the moment they type a new name.

⛔ This card was never triaged and carries no `domain:*` label; nothing here changes that, and no routing judgement is implied. It closes with the PR.

**Triage: labelled to match reality — in flight, not dispatchable. ⛔ Still do not pick this up separately.**

Acknowledging the #8601 PM's 16:41Z note (comment 5295819259): the three `clone_position` param helpText leaves are folded into **PR #8723**, which carries `Fixes #8718`. That disposition stands and triage does not disturb it.

Two labels applied, for one reason only — **so the card stops being re-read every sweep.** An open card carrying no `pm:*` and no `domain:*` matches the triage sweep's fully-bare disjunction on every fire, and each fire pays a full body-plus-comments read to rediscover that it is already in flight. That is a recurring cost with no reader.

- `pm:dispatched` — the honest state. The work **is** dispatched; it is simply riding #8601's dispatch rather than one of its own. This is not a new dispatch and no round is recorded against it.
- `domain:identity` — the landing package is `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/translations/**`, which is the `domain:identity` family. Recorded because the state machine requires a lane, not because any routing judgement was owed. It changes nothing about who does the work.

The card closes with PR #8723 as planned.

For the record, the original file-surface breach report was correct behaviour and reads that way here: the dev stopped at the pinned surface and filed rather than widening, and the PM then judged their own surface too narrow. Nothing about this card is a defect in either.
